title: Leif Erikson to Vinland, c. 1000
summary: From Brattahlíð in Greenland west across the Davis Strait to Helluland, down the Labrador coast to Markland, and on to Vinland; Leif's landfalls as the Saga of the Greenlanders names them.

events.label: Helluland
events.text: The Saga of the Greenlanders gives the name as "Flat-stone land": mountains, glaciers and slabs of rock, and no grass. It is usually taken for Baffin Island. Leif landed, looked and went on.

events.label: Markland
events.text: The "Forest land": a low, flat coast of woods and white sand beaches, usually taken for Labrador. Greenland had almost no timber of its own, so a coast of trees was worth knowing.

events.label: Vinland
events.text: Leif wintered here, in a country of self-sown wheat and grapes, the saga says, and called it Vinland. In 1960 a Norse settlement was found at L'Anse aux Meadows on Newfoundland, with a smithy and three halls; tree rings date its felled timber to exactly 1021. Whether it was Vinland itself or a base on the way is still argued.
events.source: Saga of the Greenlanders; L'Anse aux Meadows
